 Illinois saw its four-game winning streak end Friday night at the Rose Bowl. A 22-14 loss to still unbeaten No. 4 UCLA that dropped the Illini to 6-4 on the season. Ten games down with two to go, here are 10 more things our Scott Richey thinks he knows about the Illini:
 1. Katin Houser’s decision making in the face of persistent pressure from the UCLA defense was a bit problematic. The Illinois quarterback threw an interception to avoid taking a sack and then took a sack in the end zone for a safety when he should have thrown the ball away. Houser is ultimately the one who shoulders the responsibility for the ball in the air, but he wasn’t helped by how often the Bruins got in the backfield. Brandon Hansen played well enough as a fill-in guard the Illinois staff wanted to get him on the field more regularly, but tackle isn’t his strongest position. That showed Friday night.
 2. While we’re on the subject of quarterbacks, Carson Boyd was put in an impossible situation when he replaced a battered, bloodied Houser on Illinois’ final drive. The 6-foot, 190-pound sophomore hadn’t taken a single snap all night — offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. chose not to use the package built for him — but there was still a chance (albeit a small one) he could lead a game-winning drive. Nothing about how Illinois had handled UCLA’s defense changed, however, with Boyd throwing three incompletions while hurried each time.
 3. It feels like an annual event. Each year leading into the Illinois football season there’s a conversation held about how this is the year the Illini are going to use their tight ends more. The reality, particularly during Bret Bielema’s tenure as coach? The tight ends’ list of priorities starts with blocking and sometimes gets to pass catching. Tip Reiman and Tanner Arkin didn’t end up on NFL rosters because they were vertical passing threats. Reiman was drafted by the Arizona Cardinals and Arkin made the New England Patriots’ roster as an undrafted free agent because they can manhandle people at the line of scrimmage. Kaden Feagin has some of that same physicality and could turn into a dynamic blocker as he continues to adjust to his new position. But the former running back — all 6-3, 260 of him — is showing himself to be more of an offensive weapon at tight end. Three catches for 49 yards and a touchdown against UCLA isn’t otherworldly production, but is a sign Feagin can be a go-to option in the passing game.
 4. The season-ending injury to freshman running back Javari Barnett — one month after junior running back Ca’Lil Valentine suffered a similar fate — created a legitimate question around Illinois’ depth at that position. Would sophomore Cedric Wyche II or junior Murphy Clement get some (or all) of the carries Barnett had earned. The answer was … neither. Aidan Laughery and Jordan Anderson combined to rush 22 times for 66 yards, and no other running back got a touch. That seems like the likely outcome the rest of the season.
 5. Friday’s game also created a question about Illinois’ rotation at wide receiver, as Hudson Clement got hurt in the fourth quarter and was immediately put in a sling. Bielema didn’t have any injury updates immediately after the game, but the fact there was zero delay in getting Clement in a sling doesn’t bode well. The 6-1, 215-pound senior caught three passes for 62 yards against UCLA and is Illinois’ second-leading receiver this season behind Collin Dixon with 40 catches for 602 yards and one touchdown. If Clement can’t go next week against Iowa, Ty Robinson or Jershaun Newton will have to pick up the slack.
 6. It was clear who had responsibility for the blown coverage that allowed UCLA wide receiver Aidan Mizell to break free for a 54-yard touchdown on the opening drive. The next time the Illinois defense was on the field, Ben Clawson had subbed in at free safety with Tanner Heckel moving to cornerback to replace Jakwon Morris. The necessity to keep moving Heckel, who has bounced between safety and cornerback for weeks, comes down to the Illinois staff not quite trusting freshmen cornerbacks Nick Hankins Jr. and Almirian Thomas. Both are potential starter-level players, but the way Bielema has discussed the situation makes it clear they’re not quite ready for prime time.
 7. Clawson’s emergence as an every down option in the secondary in his fifth year with the program is the conclusion of quite the journey. The Arlington Heights native joined Illinois as a walk-on in 2022 and has played almost exclusively on special teams since 2023. Clawson has five tackles in the last two games after starting to get more snaps at safety, and his eight for the season quadrupled his previous career total.
 8. No player seems to have benefitted more from Illinois’ change in defensive leadership from Bobby Hauck to Roger Cooper than James Kreutz. The fifth-year linebacker had 14 tackles through the Illini’s first four games under Hauck and struggled through some of the same missed tackle issues (among others) that plagued the defense in that early stretch. Since Hauck’s departure and Cooper’s ascension to defensive play caller, Kreutz has 57 tackles and has shown more disruptive ability with five tackles for loss. His 11 tackles against UCLA marked his third double-digit in the last five games.
 9. Bielema likely won’t make any decision about the future of the Illinois defense until after the season. Despite Cooper not even getting an interim coordinator title, the reversal of fortunes for the Illini on that side of the ball in the last month have been impressive enough he’s gone from long shot candidate to get the full-time job to arguably the favorite. Take out UCLA’s safety on Friday night, and the Illinois defense has allowed just 15 points per game in the last four games.
 10. Friday’s loss to UCLA eliminated the exceedingly slim chance Illinois had at the College Football Playoff. Three losses could be workable. Four is too many. So the final two games of the regular season will help determine which bowl game the Illini wind up in next month. The ideal choice? Either a second straight year at the Music City Bowl or a return to Tampa, Fla., for the ReliaQuest Bowl. Anything but Dec. 26 at the Pinstripe Bowl in New York.
 Scott Richey covers college basketball for The News-Gazette. His email is srichey@news-gazette.com , and you can follow him on Twitter ( @srrichey ).
